title: Contextual credit velocity experiment + enterprise SQ readiness
creator: Asha Patel
description: Run a multi-armed experiment that tests credit allocation and expiry behavior tied to user credit velocity and contextual upgrade prompts. Parallel track: prepare answers and automation for the enterprise security questionnaire (SQ) items that enterprise buyers raise around trial abuse, credit accounting, and data separation for Private/Dedicated customers.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Experiment instrumented with deterministic bucketing and feature flags; 2) Dashboard showing per-cohort conversion and cost metrics; 3) One prioritized SQ appendix drafted for Sales and Legal; 4) Safety signals (abuse heuristics) enabled and tested in shadow mode.
experiment_design: We will randomly assign new signups over a 6-week window into four cohorts: Control (current 500 credits, 7-day expiry), Variant A (1000 credits, 7-day expiry), Variant B (500 credits, 14-day expiry), Variant C (velocity-topup + contextual upgrade prompt). Velocity-topup rules: if a user consumes >=60% of initial credits within first 48 hours, grant a one-time top-up of 300 credits and show an in-app upgrade prompt tailored to their usage (examples: 'You're using Redwood heavily — upgrade for predictable capacity and lower cost per token'). Bucketing to be deterministic by user_id hash; rollout via feature flag with server-side evaluation to avoid client tampering.
metrics: Primary: 30-day paid conversion rate (signup -> paid). Secondary: 7/14-day active retention, time-to-first-charge, average revenue per converted user (ARPC), per-user inference cost vs revenue (unit economics), support inquiry rate related to credits, abuse rate (accounts flagged by heuristics). Success thresholds: lift in conversion >= 10% for a variant with no >20% increase in abuse or >15% degradation in unit economics.
rollout_plan: Week 0: instrument metrics and feature flags; Week 1: run small pilot (1% of signups) to validate instrumentation; Week 2-7: ramp to target 25% of signups per cohort (control + 3 variants) achieving statistically significant sample size; Week 8: analyze, decide (rollback, iterate, or launch). Communicate experiment to Sales and Support with canned responses and SQ guidance.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Top-up variant could be abused by bot farms to drain capacity -> mitigate with rate limits (per IP and per billing fingerprint), CAPTCHA on high-velocity signups, and server-side heuristics (device fingerprint + usage pattern anomaly detection). Risk: Negative unit economics if credits far exceed conversion gains -> enforce cost guardrails and simulate per-cohort expected cost before full ramp. Risk: Enterprise buyers ask for contract language about trial credits -> coordinate with Legal to prepare SQ appendix and an upgrade path that maps credits to contract terms.
